ceiling_directive: Prove that positive TCF identification transfers from the finite strictly positive subclass to the published lm-SCM class, rather than transferring only negative counterexamples.
improvement_directive: Replace the trace-independent fiber-constancy test as the completeness engine with an ID-style colored recursion, and prove that every recursion failure returns a finite colored hedge realizable by two strictly positive same-observed, different-query lm-SCMs. Strengthen the swap result to the full legal-order confluence needed by that recursion.
critique: The delivered iff is pointwise semialgebraic constancy on a finite strictly positive subclass, obtained by quantifier elimination over the entire response-function fiber; colored fixing only discovers optional expressions and is not the source of completeness. The procedure expressly does not return a colored hedge, and the failure compiler may return only an exhaustion tag, so the advertised complete-recovery object does not deliver the graphwise sound-and-complete colored calculus motivating the note. Positive identification is not transferred to the published ambient lm-SCM class, while the claimed strict extension is only against the sufficient de Aguas criterion on the note's constructed EIPFD family. Thus the result is a narrow exact-decision baseline with positive countermodels, not a flagship graphical characterization or broadly reusable identification framework.
